_readme: What this file is: the record of what Google Cloud has to contain before
Google Sign-In can work on a real device, measured from this repository and
from public endpoints on 2026-11-02. tool/check_google_sign_in_config.dart
reads it, and the suite fails until androidClientConfirmed is true.
It contains no secret. A client id and a SHA-1 certificate fingerprint are
public identifiers: the client id is compiled into the APK and the
fingerprint is meant to be pasted into the Google console.
The two Google Cloud projects are deliberately different. 644544428760
(new-coffee-4d196) is the Firebase project that google-services.json and
lib/firebase_options.dart are generated from - it owns Cloud Messaging, and
replacing it would break push notifications. 496541472556 owns the OAuth
web client that Supabase redirects to and that the build passes as
serverClientId, so it is the only project where the Android OAuth client
can be registered. Nothing in android/ or lib/ reads default_web_client_id,
which is why the login does not need google-services.json at all; the
checker verifies that every build.
How to finish this (one step, needs the console owner):
1. console.cloud.google.com -> project 496541472556 -> APIs & Services ->
Credentials -> Create credentials -> OAuth client ID -> Android.
2. Package name: com.example.new_coffee ; SHA-1: both values in
signingCertificates below (debug and release are different
certificates; one entry per SHA-1).
3. Re-check the fingerprints after any keystore change with
./gradlew :app:printSigningFingerprints - it compares them with this
file and says MATCHES or DOES NOT MATCH.
4. Then set androidClientConfirmed to true and put the date in confirmedOn,
and sign in on a device: the refusal logged as
'[16] Account reauth failed' has to disappear.
Do not change the web client Supabase is configured with, and do not create
a third project for this - the evidence below says the existing one works.
evidence: GET that authorize URL with no cookies -> Google accepts the client and
continues to the consent flow (requestPath=/signin/oauth/v3/consent, no
authError). The same request with one digit of the client id changed ->
invalid_client. So the web client exists and its Supabase callback is
registered: the provider is configured, the missing piece is not there.
emulator-5554, 2026-11-02 00:36, debug APK built from this branch:
That is Credential Manager refusing an app it cannot match to an Android
OAuth client, which is what this record is waiting to be marked done.
